subject: Priv. Offer: Itemized SKUs vs Flat Fee — Channel Margin alignment
messages:
From: Maya Patel <maya.patel@clearhealth.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@clearhealth.ai
Date: 2027-05-16T08:12:00Z
Subject: Pricing structure question — itemized SKUs vs flat fee

Hi Hannah + Ben,

Really enjoyed the demo yesterday — the team is excited. Procurement has a practical question as we shape the private offer: would you recommend an itemized SKU-based private offer (metered SKU lines for generation/embeddings/support) vs a single flat-fee enterprise SKU for our 12-month committed purchase?

Key asks from our side:
- Example commercial math (list price -> private offer discount) for both approaches
- Expected channel margin/pass-through for our reseller (HealthLaunch) and how that changes the net to Redwood
- Any operational differences / invoicing implications we should anticipate

I've attached our counterproposal for context (summary of expected usage and preferred payment terms). Can you share a short note with the tradeoffs and a recommended path? We're targeting a decision by end of week.

Thanks,
Maya
Maya Patel
Head of Procurement | ClearHealth AI
Attachments: clearhealth-counterproposal.pdf
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Patel <maya.patel@clearhealth.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-16T10:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Pricing structure question — itemized SKUs vs flat fee

Hi Maya — thanks for the clear write-up and the timelines. Looping in Ben (deal lead) and Irene (channel ops) to confirm the channel/pass-through mechanics.

Short take (high level):
- Itemized SKUs gives better per-unit economics and more predictable passback calculation for HealthLaunch; easier to align discounts per SKU (e.g., gen vs embeddings).
- Flat-fee simplifies procurement and invoicing on their side, but typically requires a higher net discount to approximate the same net partner margin — which compresses Redwood's revenue unless we structure minimum commits and usage bands.

Action items: Ben/Irene — can you review the attached draft pricing grid I'm preparing (will send v3) and advise:
- Recommended reseller pass-through % for an early-adopter proof-of-concept vs enterprise commit
- Whether we can do an itemized private offer that includes an invoice-level ‘reseller credit’ line so HealthLaunch can be paid separately without complicating ClearHealth's invoicing

Maya — we'll follow up with concrete numbers by EOD tomorrow.

Best,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Maya Patel <maya.patel@clearhealth.ai>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-16T11:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Pricing structure question — itemized SKUs vs flat fee

Thanks Hannah — quick notes from the deal perspective:

- Prefer itemized SKUs for this account. It keeps list-price transparency and lets us tier discounts by SKU/usage (helps protect revenue where embeddings-heavy usage can be higher-margin).
- Suggested reseller pass-through: 18–20% for early-adopter POC (no minimum), 15% for committed enterprise flat-fee deals (with a 12-month minimum).
- If ClearHealth prefers flat-fee, we should model a blended list price that results in equivalent revenue to the itemized approach and then apply a 15% reseller margin — otherwise Redwood net drops materially.

I've attached the latest pricing grid (redwood-pricing-grid-v3.xlsx) with two sensitivities (itemized vs blended-flat). See rows 12–22 for the reseller-impact column.

Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood-pricing-grid-v3.xlsx
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Maya Patel <maya.patel@clearhealth.ai>
Date: 2027-05-17T09:15:00Z
Subject: Re: Pricing structure question — itemized SKUs vs flat fee

Hi all — operational considerations from channel/finance ops:

- Itemized private offer + reseller pass-through: we can issue the private offer to ClearHealth with line-item prices. HealthLaunch can be paid via separate reseller invoice; ops will require a partner-submission form and PO number from HealthLaunch for rebate processing.
- Flat-fee private offer: invoicing is simpler (single line), but we must capture usage bands in a side letter for true-up (we typically do quarterly true-ups). This is important for tax/tier reporting and for avoiding month-to-month over/under-payments to the reseller.
- Recommend including a 90-day true-up clause and a clear escrow/retention for usage credits (standard dev/test cushion of 5%).

I will coordinate the partner payment flow with Finance once the commercial terms are decided. If we go itemized, Finance prefers the reseller margin to be handled as a tracked commission (not a discount on the private offer) — this helps revenue recognition and partner reporting.

Irene
Irene Choi
Partner Operations | Redwood Inference
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Patel <maya.patel@clearhealth.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-19T15:40:00Z
Subject: Re: Pricing structure question — itemized SKUs vs flat fee

Hi Maya — thanks for your patience. Summary recommendation and next steps below.

Recommendation (two-track, choose one):

1) Itemized SKU private offer (recommended for PT/POC -> scale):
- Line items: Gen per-1K-tokens, Embeddings per-1K (see attached grid).
- Reseller pass-through: 18% standard for POC (HealthLaunch) — Redwood will record this as commission (not a discount) for clean revenue recognition.
- Terms: net-30 invoicing to ClearHealth; HealthLaunch paid monthly on submitted partner invoice; 90-day quarterly true-up; 5% dev/test cushion.

2) Blended flat-fee enterprise private offer (if ClearHealth needs single invoice):
- Blended list to match expected annualized spend (we modeled a blended list that preserves ~98% of itemized net to Redwood).
- Reseller margin: 15% (applies to flat-fee). 12-month minimum commit required. Quarterly true-up still applies.

Next steps:
- Please confirm which option ClearHealth prefers. Once confirmed, we will:
  - Finalize private offer doc and partner commission lines (Ben)
  - Create the partner payment flow and true-up schedule (Irene)
  - Issue the private-offer link and DocuSign to ClearHealth for signature

Maya — attaching the pricing grid and a redline-ready private offer template for review. If you want, Ben and I can run a 15–20 minute walk-through tomorrow to step through the numbers.

Best,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
